prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules recruit ubiquitin ligases to destroy chosen proteins, through PROTACs and through the molecular mechanism of cereblon-based glue degraders

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation is a genuinely new chemical principle: a small molecule acts catalytically and event-drivenly by inducing proximity between a ligase and a target, rather than occupying a binding site. It is physical-chemical in character (ternary-complex cooperativity, linker design, interfacial protein-protein recognition), it has been validated by structures and by many independent groups, and it has produced a large clinical pipeline. Seven of eight opening ballots placed it in the top three, which is unusual breadth, but that is not what persuades me. What does is that the Crews and Deshaies concept and the Handa identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target explain two complementary halves of one mechanism, and a three-person prize can honestly cover both. I moved B020 above my own opening first choice (B024) because the case for it is more mature and more settled as chemistry.
statement.case_against: No PROTAC has yet been approved, so the claim of transformed medicine rests on trial outcomes still to come. The configuration also excludes Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto and Ito, any of whom can be argued to be decisive, and the bifunctional and molecular-glue strands have different inventors and different histories, so a single citation risks looking like a compromise rather than one discovery. My own opening favourite, biomolecular phase separation (B024), is conceptually deeper for the physical chemistry of cells, but its physiological relevance is still contested, which is why I do not press it as the lead.

responses.point: Daniel ranks B020 first with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, arguing that Ciulli's structure-based VHL ligands and ternary-complex work were decisive and that the cereblon glue lineage may need separate recognition or be left out.
responses.response: I agree on the importance of B020 and on Ciulli's contribution to rational design, but I would put Handa in the third place. Without the cereblon discovery the thalidomide-type glues remain a mystery and the field would be PROTACs only; Ciulli's work refines a modality that Crews and Deshaies had already established. I accept this is a real judgment call, and if the committee wanted to emphasise the design chemistry over the glue mechanism, Ciulli in place of Handa would be defensible. I would not drop the glue strand altogether, since it is the part most closely tied to a drug already used in patients.

responses.point: Johan ranks Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics first because the attribution to two people is unusually clean and the method unified electronic structure and nuclear motion for condensed-phase chemistry.
responses.response: The attribution argument is strong and I agree B061 is the cleanest case on the shortlist for who deserves credit. My reservation is about reach and timing: its influence is largely methodological within theory, whereas the impact of B020 has also reached how drugs are conceived. Having a clean pair does not by itself make a prize more urgent than one with a harder but richer allocation problem. I would keep B061 as a serious option for a later year rather than let clarity of credit decide between candidates, and I do not think it should displace B020 now.

responses.point: Peter ranks Pd-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling (Buchwald and Hartwig) first on its clean pair attribution and broad synthetic and pharmaceutical use, while noting overlap with the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
responses.response: I share his own worry about overlap: the 2010 prize already recognised palladium cross-coupling as a concept, and C-N coupling is an extension of that logic with a very high practical impact, instead of a new chemical idea. By comparison, induced proximity is a different mode of action altogether. I take the point that a synthetic method that every medicinal chemist uses daily is easy to evaluate and has settled impact, so I would be open to B044 later, but not ahead of B020, and I do not see enough novelty to lead this year.

responses.point: Andrei ranks base editing (Liu with Komor and Gaudelli) first, as a new defined molecular transformation by deaminase chemistry without double-strand breaks, with Liu clearly leading.
responses.response: Liu's role is not in doubt and the chemistry of editing a single base is elegant. I am less convinced about putting two trainees on the prize, and the independent Target-AID work of Nishida and Kondo complicates priority more than the opening ballots suggest. The proximity to the 2020 CRISPR prize also leaves a risk that this will be seen as a follow-up to that award. I place it behind B020 for those reasons, though not far behind, and a Liu-only or Liu-led prize could be worth another look once priority is better understood.

responses.point: Heiner, the chair, ranks B020 first with Crews, Deshaies and Handa and flags uncertainty about whether the prize should cover PROTACs, glues or both, and whether Ciulli, Gray and Sakamoto might be argued as decisive.
responses.response: I agree with his configuration and with his framing that the open question is the scope of the citation. My view is that it should cover both strands, because the cereblon mechanism and the PROTAC concept together define what event-driven degradation pharmacology is. I disagree mildly with the idea that Ciulli or Gray are decisive for the founding discovery: they are major developers of the field after its concept was set, and a three-person limit forces a line to be drawn somewhere. Sakamoto as first author of the 2001 paper is the hardest omission and I do not think the committee should be comfortable about it.

uncertainties: Whether the citation should cover PROTACs and molecular glues together or only one strand, and how much weight the absence of an approved PROTAC should carry.
Fair treatment of Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto and Ito under a three-person limit.
Whether biomolecular phase separation (B024) is mature enough despite continuing disputes about physiological relevance, and whether Pappu and Mittag would need credit with it.
Whether the 2023 Medicine prize for mRNA should weigh against lipid nanoparticle delivery (B010), and who among six or more inventors would be credited.
statement.conflict_note: I work on lipid self-assembly and lipid-protein co-assembly, which is close to the lipid nanoparticle candidate (B010) and to biomolecular condensates (B024, where I rank first in my opening ballot, and where amyloid and condensate work overlaps with mine), so I would be cautious about leading a decision on those two and would state this to the committee. I also sit on the committee with Lund colleagues Heiner Linke and Peter Somfai; no personal connection to any proposed laureate is apparent from my profile.
